page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-standard-4 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance belonging to the n2d server family. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor using the x86_64 architecture. The instance is configured with 16 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or integrated GPU accelerators, and it does not offer complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks reveal a distinct contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The AMD EPYC 7B13 processor delivers strong single-core CPU performance in stress-ng tests, placing in the top 25%. However, multi-core CPU performance and Geekbench multi-core scores fall into the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth tests show average performance for large-block read and write operations, but small-block cached reads are weak. Cryptographic capabilities are supported by hardware-accelerated instructions such as AES, VAES, and SHA_NI, which is reflected in average scores for Passmark CPU encryption and single-threaded gzip compression.

The primary tradeoff of the n2d-standard-4 is its limited multi-threaded scaling, as evidenced by poor multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and weak database operation scores. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, this instance offers a dedicated hardware profile suitable for entry-level workloads that require consistent CPU allocation without the overhead of high-end multi-core configurations. It is best suited for general-purpose workloads such as light web serving, single-threaded text processing, and basic application hosting where high multi-threaded throughput is not critical.
description: Google Cloud Platform n2d-standard-4 is a general-purpose virtual machine configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs and 16 GB of RAM, powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor on the x86_64 architecture. It features 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core and 32 MB of L3 cache. The instance lacks local storage and GPU acceleration. Benchmarks indicate strong single-core CPU performance, ranking in the top 25% in stress-ng tests, though multi-core performance and memory bandwidth for small blocks remain weak. Cryptographic operations perform at average levels due to hardware-accelerated AES and SHA_NI support. Given its balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and dedicated CPU allocation, this instance is qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads that do not require heavy multi-threading. It is best suited for general-purpose applications, light web serving, and single-threaded processing tasks.
